blocks.x: Products enforce; architecture decides where trust dies.
Zero-trust is an architecture, not a purchase. Trust-tier migration sequences the estate so value lands in months, not years.
Workload identity (SPIFFE-class) closes the service-to-service trust gap humans ignore.
Evidence packs mapped to ISO 27001/SOC 2 turn certification into collection.

Where it breaks in practice: product-first thinking — tools purchased faster than architecture is decided, so coverage overlaps in some places and leaks in others while the estate grows more complex, not safer.
The serious opposition goes: the architecture-first thesis can drift into analysis paralysis while the estate keeps growing. Zero-trust lands in order of blast radius, not in order of elegance.

In delivery, this thesis becomes a specific discipline: we harden the paths the work takes: workload identity, least-privilege access, encrypted data in use, and an evidence trail the auditor can walk alone. Every program in the Cyber & Zero-Trust domain carries the same obligations — a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
Bring zero-trust is an architecture, not a purchase to a 45-minute briefing with the practice lead — your metric, our method, and an honest read on feasibility.
